intro.title: Test useFetch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test for a custom Angular hook called useFetch, which handles data fetching in a component. You'll learn how to write unit tests using Jasmine and Angular's TestBed to verify that the hook correctly manages loading states, successful data retrieval, and error handling. The core concept involves mocking HTTP requests with HttpClientTestingModule and HttpTestingController to simulate API responses without making real network calls. By the end, you'll understand how to test asynchronous logic and ensure your custom hooks work reliably in an Angular application.
intro.usecase: Testing custom hooks like useFetch is essential for building reliable data-driven applications in Angular. In real-world products, this pattern appears when validating data fetching logic for dashboard widgets, admin panels displaying user statistics, or e-commerce product listings with filters. Developers must ensure these hooks handle loading states, errors, and data transformations correctly to prevent UI inconsistencies. Proper testing prevents bugs in critical user flows like search results, financial data displays, or real-time notifications.
